prf:unified-iterative-correction:
Proof Proof of unified iterative correction. By prop:mass-coefficient-shadow-price, the BW coefficient of partition \lambda is the LP-dual variable u_\lambda^* = C_\lambda \cdot S_\lambda(Z, N, A). The categorical scale C_\lambda = m_e \cdot H_q(\lambda) (the q-hook product over the Young diagram of \lambda) is the universal constant determined by the partition algebra, with no nuclear data; the scaling function S_\lambda(Z, N, A) is realised at each step as \ln|\mathrm{tr}\,\mathbf{M}_\lambda^{(0..A)}| - \ln d_\lambda via the Young seminormal representation.

For \lambda = (2,2) \vdash 4 this recovers the dedicated Wigner identity (prop:wigner-np-pairing): H_q((2,2)) = [3]_q \cdot [2]_q^2; for \lambda = (2,1) \vdash 3 it reproduces the volume / surface / Coulomb decomposition through their image under the Wedderburn embedding — a step this proof does not discharge, and which the corpus still cannot supply.

The obstruction is one of shape. The Wedderburn embedding is a concrete construction, but it has type \bigoplus_\lambda M_{f^\lambda} \to M_{n!}: it assembles blocks into one matrix rather than splitting one block's scalar C_{(2,1)} into three coefficients. The landing in M_{n!} is additionally conditional on the RSK identity \sum_\lambda (f^\lambda)^2 = n!, carried as a named hypothesis and discharged by nothing here.

That objection is now a theorem, not a remark . The naive form — "three independent coefficients cannot come from one scalar" — is false, since one real encodes three set-theoretically. Under linearity, which this corpus already assumes for the Markov trace, it is true: that trace factors through the block traces, so a functional of that form supported at a single \lambda is exactly c_\lambda \cdot \operatorname{tr}(x_\lambda) — one coefficient against one number — and any three such are linearly dependent, with an explicit witness .

This does not make the clause false; it rules out the route the clause names, whenever that route is linear, factors through the Markov trace, and is localised at (2,1). It also says where the room is, which is the more useful half: f^{(2,1)} = 2, so the block is M_2(\mathbb{R}) — four real dimensions, of which the trace reads one. The information wanted is present in the block and destroyed by tracing it — itself now a theorem: whenever a block has dimension at least 2 there are distinct decompositions on which every block trace agrees, so every trace-factoring functional, the Markov trace included, takes the same value on both. Instantiating that at (2,1) needs f^{(2,1)} = 2; that value is established (via the Frame–Robinson–Thrall hook-length formula), so the instance at (2,1) holds unconditionally. The general theorems keep the bound as a hypothesis because they are about any block of dimension \geq 2. The boundary is real: f^{(1,1)} = 1, so at the charge shape the block is its trace and none of this applies. A derivation reading the block rather than its trace is not blocked by any of this — and that is now constructive rather than merely permitted: there exist three linearly independent block-reading functionals at (2,1), the exact complement of the three trace-factoring ones being dependent. It does not identify those three with volume, surface and Coulomb; three independent functionals existing is a necessary condition for such a match, not evidence of one. So the clause is still an open obligation, not a derivation; for higher partitions it adds the form-factor, pn-correlation, and {[3,2,1]} pn-invisible corrections.

By the Markov-trace normalization (the per-level budget is the Hecke-level scale [k]_q!, k fixed), the dual shadow prices satisfy a single budget constraint per Hecke level; by Frobenius reciprocity (prop:mass-coefficient-shadow-price, branching corollary), shadow prices at level k+1 are determined by those at level k. Telescoping per-step log-trace differences across k = 1, \ldots, A yields the closed-form B_\lambda.

The Kerov q-hook walk [kerov1996] gives the iterative Markov-chain interpretation of \mathrm{tr}\,\mathbf{M}_\lambda^{(0..k)} as a transition kernel on the Young lattice; the Féray–Méliot q-Plancherel CLT [feray-meliot2012] guarantees the asymptotic convergence of the accumulator at rate O(1/\sqrt{A}) across Hecke levels.

The three legacy mechanisms specialise:

  • deuteron (A = 2, dedicated \alpha_{\mathrm{Borromean}} \cdot \hat V_e): the A = 2 slice of the LP-dual accumulator, dominated by the (2,1) and (2,2) shadow prices;
  • knot factor (A = 3, 4, dedicated a(N) = 1 - h^2, (1 - h^2)^2): the A = 3, 4 slices of the LP-dual accumulator, where the (2,1) and (3,1) contributions reproduce the figure-eight and Borromean amphicheiral factors;
  • Wigner energy (k = 4, dedicated -\Delta_W \cdot T(T+1)/A): the k = 4 self-conjugate shadow price \lambda = (2,2), which vanishes on isolated pn crossings (extremal cancellation, prop:confined-knot-binding) but is nonzero on collective pn patterns. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) no self-conjugate partition beyond k = 4 can contribute: self-conjugacy forces \ell(\lambda) = \lambda_1, so the row cap \ell(\lambda) \leq 2 admits only (1), (2,1) and (2,2), and a block with \tilde w_\lambda = 0 has C_\lambda = 0 and hence u_\lambda^* = 0 at every (Z, N) — the vanishing is upstream of the scaling function, so no S_\lambda restores it.

\square

Algorithm summary (one block, no special cases, A = 1 onward):

    H_q(λ)   = ∏_{x∈λ} [h_x]_q

prop:frobenius-self-duality-forces-lp-du: Proposition Frobenius self-duality of (H_n(R,q),\tau) forces \tau-extraction to produce LP-dual variables. Let I_n \subset H_n(R,q) be the radical of the Markov trace \tau, the sum of the Wedderburn blocks V_\lambda with y_\lambda = 0. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) these are the shapes with three or more rows, so I_n = 0 for n \le 2 and H_n/I_n = TL_n(q). The trace descends to a non-degenerate symmetric bilinear pairing on TL_n(q). This makes (TL_n(q),\tau) a Frobenius algebra, hence canonically isomorphic to its R-linear dual. Under this isomorphism, the primal LP variable x \in TL_n and the dual LP variable u \in TL_n^* live in the same space, and the Observation Frame \mathrm{Obs}_\tau(a) := \tau(a \cdot -) extracts the shadow-price representative of every observable.
prf:frobenius-self-duality-forces-lp-dua:
Proof Proof of frobenius self duality forces lp dual extraction. Step 1: Frobenius pairing. The Markov trace \tau : H_n(R,q) \to R satisfies \tau(ab) = \tau(ba) for all a,b \in H_n, and \tau = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda by the Wedderburn trace identity. On a block with y_\lambda \neq 0 the pairing (a,b) \mapsto y_\lambda \operatorname{tr}(a_\lambda b_\lambda) is the non-degenerate matrix-trace pairing; on a block with y_\lambda = 0 it vanishes identically. So the radical of \langle a,b\rangle_\tau := \tau(ab) is I_n = \bigoplus_{y_\lambda = 0} \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda). At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the weights are y_{(3)} = (q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2, y_{(2,1)} = q^2/(q^2+1)^2 and y_{(1^3)} = 0 at n = 3, and in general every shape with three or more rows has y_\lambda = 0; so \tau is degenerate on H_n for n \ge 3. It descends to a non-degenerate symmetric pairing on TL_n(q) = H_n/I_n, making (TL_n(q), \tau) a Frobenius algebra in the sense of Frobenius (1903) and Nakayama (1939). Steps 2–5 are carried out on TL_n(q); read H_n there as TL_n.

Step 2: Self-duality isomorphism. The map

  \Phi_\tau : H_n(R,q) \longrightarrow H_n(R,q)^*,
  \quad a \mapsto \big(b \mapsto \tau(ab)\big)

is an isomorphism of R-modules (and a bimodule isomorphism when both sides carry the regular bimodule structure). This is the canonical Frobenius self-duality.

Step 3: Operator-selection LP under self-duality. The operator-selection LP at level n has primal:

  \min_{x \in H_n} \tau(\Theta \cdot x)
  \quad \text{s.t.} \quad
  \tau(\mathbf{1} \cdot x) = n_{\mathrm{target}}, \;\;
  \tau(\pi_\lambda \cdot x) \geq 0 \;\; \forall \lambda

where \Theta is the cost operator (knot-energy weight) and \pi_\lambda is the central idempotent for block V_\lambda.

The dual program is

  \max_{u_0, u_\lambda \geq 0} n_{\mathrm{target}} u_0
  \quad \text{s.t.} \quad
  u_0 \mathbf{1} + \sum_\lambda u_\lambda \pi_\lambda
  \;\preceq_\tau\; \Theta

where \preceq_\tau denotes the partial order induced by the Frobenius pairing: a \preceq_\tau b \iff \tau(c \cdot (b - a)) \geq 0 for all c \succeq_\tau 0.

Step 4: Primal-dual coincidence (under standard LP hypotheses). Under \Phi_\tau, the primal feasible set P = \{x \in H_n : \tau(\pi_\lambda \cdot x) \geq 0\} is \Phi_\tau-isomorphic to the dual feasible cone D = \{u : u \succeq_\tau 0\}. The cost functional x \mapsto \tau(\Theta \cdot x) is, under \Phi_\tau, identified with the dual objective u \mapsto \langle u, \Theta \rangle. Strong duality holds whenever the standard finite- dimensional LP regularity conditions are met — primal feasibility and primal boundedness (or, equivalently for the canonical operator-selection LP of Knot operator selection as linear program with LP duality, existence of a strictly feasible point, i.e. Slater's condition). For the per-atom operator-selection LP these hypotheses are verified by direct construction in Knot operator selection as linear program with LP duality; the proposition above adds structurally that the primal- dual identification itself does not require additional analytic argument because the Frobenius pairing is non- degenerate. Strong duality + the Frobenius identification together imply the \tau-extraction is the dual map.

Step 5: τ-extraction is the dual map. The Observation Frame \mathrm{Obs}_\tau : H_n(R,q) \to H_n(R,q)^* defined by \mathrm{Obs}_\tau(a) = \tau(a \cdot -) is \Phi_\tau. Therefore, an observable produced by τ-extraction is, by definition, a dual-space element.

Corollary. Every coefficient c_\lambda \in \mathbb{R} that arises as a τ-extracted observable from a Frobenius-positivity-constrained LP is a shadow price u_\lambda^* of the corresponding constraint. This is not a derivation; it is the structure of the observation frame in a Frobenius-self-dual category. \square

Corollary (mass-formula coefficients are LP-dual variables). By mass-coefficient-shadow-price, every QOU mass-formula coefficient C_\lambda at every Hecke level k is the τ-extraction of a shadow price; by the proposition above, this is the only form a τ-extracted observable can take in a Frobenius-self-dual category. The mass formula is therefore canonically a sum of LP-dual variables:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \sum_\ell u^{(\ell)*}

where u^{(\ell)*} is the optimal LP-dual at filtration level \ell (see mass-formula-iterative-lp-dual).
rem:frobenius-self-duality-forces-lp-dua: Remark Categorical content: self-duality of \mathbf{Rep}(H_n) behind the LP dual. The Frobenius self-duality holds at the categorical level: the rigid monoidal category \mathbf{Rep}(H_n(R,q)) is self-dual under the \tau-pairing, and \tau is precisely the categorical trace \mathrm{tr}_C on the unit object. The "primal vs. dual" distinction in the LP is a K-theoretic shadow of the categorical self-duality; there is no other choice.
prop:subset-cumulant-recursion:
Proposition Subset cumulants of the bond model: reconstruction, the c_k-only recursion, and vanishing across a split. Let L be a function on subsets S of the A nucleons of an atomic braid with L(\varnothing) = 0, and define its Möbius cumulants over the Boolean lattice by the recursion

  \mathrm{cum}(S) \;=\; L(S) \;-\; \sum_{T \subsetneq S} \mathrm{cum}(T).

Then, with no further hypothesis on L:

  1. (Reconstruction.) \displaystyle \sum_{T \subseteq S} \mathrm{cum}(T) = L(S) for every S.
  2. (The c_k-only recursion.) If L(S) depends only on |S|, say L(S) = f(|S|), then \mathrm{cum}(S) = c_{|S|} where 
      c_k \;=\; f(k) \;-\; \sum_{j<k} \binom{k}{j}\, c_j .
  3. (Mixed cumulants vanish across an additive split.) If the nucleons split as \mathcal{A} \sqcup \mathcal{B} and L(S) = L(S \cap \mathcal{A}) + L(S \cap \mathcal{B}) for every S, then \mathrm{cum}(S) = 0 whenever S meets both \mathcal{A} and \mathcal{B}.

What it is for

The bond model of binding reads the many-body content of a nucleus off the Markov trace: with bonds placed among the nucleons in S, in the interleaved order the canonical interface composition fixes, one sets L(S) = \log\bigl(\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{free}} / \mathrm{tr}_S\bigr) and reads the genuine k-body term as the order-k cumulant. Item 1 is what makes the cumulants a decomposition of the full L rather than a rearrangement of it; item 3 is what makes them cumulants in the standard sense -- independence kills every mixed one -- and it is the property that turns the Markov trace's multiplicativity on split links (an unbonded nucleon is a separate component, contributing equally to numerator and denominator) into additivity of L on disjoint bonded parts.

Item 2 is the working tool. For an exchangeable system -- every nucleon the same, so L(S) sees only |S| -- the 2^A - A - 1 subset traces at 3A strands collapse to A - 1 scalar inputs f(k) = L_k, each of which can be computed in its own minimal system of 3k strands because L(S) does not see nucleons outside S. At A = 6 that is five trace pairs, one of them at n = 18, in place of fifty-seven traces at n = 18; it is the difference between an order-six cumulant existing and not.

What is a theorem and what is a measurement

The three items are algebra, true for every set function on every commutative ring, and are proved. The two facts that make the bond model an instance -- that the homonuclear L(S) depends only on |S|, and that it does not see nucleons outside S -- are properties of this particular trace. They are established at 200-bit precision (residuals at the working floor, \sim 10^{-59}, at A = 3, 4, 5), and they are not proved: the Markov-trace properties available are cyclicity and single-generator conjugation, not the split-link tensor rule, and the band routing of a far bond sits between other letters where conjugation invariance does not reach.
rem:body-number-expansion-classical-floo:
Remark The body-number expansion has a classical floor: no power counting in q - 1. The subset-cumulant recursion reads the genuine k-body content of a nucleus off the Markov trace as the order-k Möbius cumulant of L(S) = \log(\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{free}}/\mathrm{tr}_S). A natural question is whether these cumulants are ordered in the deformation parameter \varepsilon = q - 1: whether the k-body term is smaller than the (k-1)-body term by a power of \varepsilon, so that the body-number expansion would carry a power counting of the kind an effective field theory organises its operators by. This remark records that it does not, and why.

The bond factors at the classical point. With the bonds placed by the canonical interface composition, the ratio \mathrm{tr}_S/\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{free}} is a product of interface factors, one per bond, each of the form z + d: the Markov parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2} + 1) of the trace selection, plus a correction d depending on the kind of the interface (proton–proton, proton–neutron, neutron–neutron). Expanded at q = 1 + \varepsilon the three bond factors are

  \tfrac12 + \varepsilon + \tfrac14 \varepsilon^{2}, \qquad
  \tfrac12 + 0\cdot\varepsilon + \tfrac34 \varepsilon^{2}, \qquad
  \tfrac12 - \varepsilon + \tfrac54 \varepsilon^{2}

to second order, and the point is the common constant term: z(1) = 1/2, and every d vanishes at \varepsilon = 0. At the classical point every bond factor is 1/2, whatever its kind.

The cumulant does not vanish. Write f_e for a bond factor and g_e = f_e - 1 for its Mayer variable; the connected three-body cumulant of the multiplicative assembly is minus the third Ursell function, b_3 = -\varphi^{T}_{3}(g_{12}, g_{13}, g_{23}) with \varphi^{T}_{3} = g_{12}g_{13}g_{23} + g_{12}g_{13} + g_{12}g_{23} + g_{13}g_{23}, the sum over the connected spanning graphs on three vertices. At the classical point g_e = -1/2 for every bond, so

  b_3\bigl(\tfrac12, \tfrac12, \tfrac12\bigr) \;=\; -\Bigl(-\tfrac18 + \tfrac34\Bigr) \;=\; -\tfrac58 \;\neq\; 0 ,

and the same computation for four bodies gives b_4 = 79/64. The three-body term therefore has \varepsilon-valuation zero: it is not suppressed relative to the two-body term by any power of \varepsilon, and the body-number expansion at fixed q is a lattice-gas cluster expansion with weights of order one. Its convergence is a question about the size of the Mayer variables, not about a small parameter. (For the mixed triple of one bond of each kind the \varepsilon-series of b_3 begins -5/8 + 0\cdot\varepsilon + \tfrac{35}{16}\varepsilon^{2}; the vanishing of the linear term is a property of that triple, not a general one.)

What the corpus already knew, in another guise. The classical floor of the trace difference \Delta = \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{free}} - \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{atom}}, the coefficient c_0 = 2^{-A} - 2^{1 - 2A} of \varepsilon^{0}, is nonzero for every A \geq 2; it is the same fact seen through the difference rather than through the cumulants.

What is ordered. The expansion of the framework that is geometric is the jet tower: the transfer operator is a series in \hbar_q^{2n} over jet levels n with remainder ratio q^{-2}, so that the local single-jet contribution leads and corrections form a geometric series. The framework's small parameter counts jet level, not body number. An effective-field-theory reading of the corpus is therefore a statement about the jet tower — the truncation order of the ladder, the descended level-zero holonomy — and not about the many-body assembly, whose expansion parameter is the bond weight itself.

Scope. This excludes an ordering in \varepsilon, on the strength of the identity z(1) = 1/2; it is a structural exclusion of that ordering and nothing more. It does not exclude an ordering of the body-number expansion in some other quantity, and it does not bear on the sign question for b_3, which is a question about the bond factors at the physical point.
rem:canonical-trace-factorises-over-chai:
Remark The canonical mass trace factorises over the chain: the bond constants are -\log(z+d) and the canonical closure carries no many-body binding. The chain form has an algebraic consequence that is stronger than the topological one. Write the canonical Hecke word as \prod_i p_i(\sigma_i), one polynomial per generator in Coxeter order -- the averaged letters sit inside the power of their own generator, so this needs no branch to be chosen. Then the normalised Markov trace on H_{3A} is the product of two-strand traces,

  \mathrm{tr}_M\Bigl(\prod_i p_i(\sigma_i)\Bigr)
  \;=\;
  \prod_i \bigl[\,w_+\,p_i(q) + w_-\,p_i(-q^{-1})\,\bigr],
  \qquad
  w_+ = \frac{[3]_q}{[3]_q+1},\quad w_- = \frac{1}{[3]_q+1},

because a closed braid whose word is a product of sub-words on strand sets overlapping in one strand is a connected sum, and the Markov trace -- like every multiplicative link invariant -- is multiplicative under connected sum, not only under the split union of the KS shortcut. Each interface generator carries the single letter \sigma + d, whose two-strand trace is

  w_+(q + d) + w_-(-q^{-1} + d) \;=\; z + d,
  \qquad z = \frac{q^3}{q^2+1},

so the free-minus-atom log-ratio is exactly a sum over the A-1 interfaces:

  L(Z,N) \;=\; \sum_{\text{interfaces}} -\log(z + d_i),
  \qquad
  L_{pp} = -\log z,\quad
  L_{nn} = -\log(z - h) = \log\bigl(q(q^2+1)\bigr),\quad
  L_{pn} = -\log(z + d_{pn}).

Measured

At 200 bits, with q from the fifty-digit aether value, the full H_{3A} Markov trace of the canonical word against the product of two-strand factors: ^2H (n=6) 2.3\times10^{-59}, ^3H and ^3He (n=9) 3.1\times10^{-59}, ^4He (n=12) 4.0\times10^{-59}; the Jones polynomial of the closure equals \prod_i V(T(2,e_i)) exactly on both classical branches for A \le 4. The three constants -\log(z+d) reproduce the binding arc's bond constants -- measured there in H_6 -- to all sixty digits.

What it means for the binding gap

The linear-chain closed form B_{\mathrm{sym}} = a\,[(Z-1)L_{pp} + L_{pn} + (N-1)L_{nn}], which the proof of that result took as its named structural input, is a corollary of the topology: connected sum \Rightarrow multiplicative trace \Rightarrow additive L. The canonical closure therefore carries no many-body binding at all -- not by measurement, by theorem. The many-body cumulants the binding arc found (c_3 < 0, c_4 < 0, c_5 > 0, the order-six datum) belong to the all-pairs bond model, whose band-routed bonds interleave generators across blocks and destroy the chain form. With \alpha = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) = 4.185981 MeV the chain gives ^4He 8.6817 MeV against B_{\mathrm{AME}} = 28.2957, namely 31\,\%; the missing 69\,\% is absent from the canonical closure because a connected sum has nothing to put there. Any closure that carries genuinely many-body binding must fail to be composite -- non-split, prime, with the kind of irreducibly multi-component linking the Borromean rings have and this chain does not. That is the precise form of "the missing binding is not in the bond graph", and it says which topology the search has to move to.

The affine law also disposes of the obvious repair. Any modification acting as an interface offset -- a convention change, a fractional twist insertion q^{2c(\lambda)/n} -- has bond constant -\log(z+d) with no trace to run, so invert it: closing ^4He on the chain with a common offset needs -\log(z+d) = 2.253212, i.e. d = -0.507627 = -2.4281\,h. The algebra's letters supply d \in \{0, -h/2, d_{pn}, -h\}, so d/h \in [-1, 0]: the required offset is 2.43\times more negative than the most negative letter that exists. No interface offset can close the gap.

The quantity L itself is a free-energy difference over the Markov state sum; that it is the binding energy is a separate and open claim.

The stated form assumes the grouped intra ordering; the conclusion does not

Writing the word as \prod_i p_i(\sigma_i) — one polynomial per generator — requires each generator's letters to be contiguous. That is a property of how the word is assembled, not of the chain topology. The canonical atom word is assembled that way (all of the \sigma_0 chain, then all of the \sigma_1 chain), which is why the identity measures exact above. In contrast, the alternating Borromean builder lays each nucleon's six confinement letters down alternating, as the (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 its own source comment always named — the Borromean braid \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}, identified against its closed form to 5\times10^{-60}. Same letter multiset, different order, and it does not satisfy the per-generator form: that fails by 2.8\times at A = 2, rising to 13.3\times at A = 4.

A distinction worth keeping. Grouped and alternating describe the arrangement of six letters inside the eleven-letter intra block, not the block itself. That block is not \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} under either arrangement and cannot be: two of its eleven letters are averaged, \sigma - (h/2)\cdot 1, which is outside the image of \rho : B_n \to H_n(q), so it is not a braid at all and has no single closure to name. One proton: 1.145759692457300870 grouped, 0.629328402202921918 alternating, against 0.998562163836787266 for the bare six-letter \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} — three distinct objects.

The factorisation survives this. The load-bearing step is connected-sum multiplicativity, which is blind to letter order inside a summand, and it is measured to survive the reordering exactly: \mathrm{tr}_M(\text{chain}) = \prod_k \mathrm{tr}_M(\text{intra}_k)\prod_i(z+d_i). So the interface factors, the three bond constants and L itself are identical under both orderings — to \sim 10^{-60} at A = 2, 3, 4 — and the "no many-body binding" conclusion holds for either word. What is ordering-specific is the stronger per-generator statement.

The same caveat applies one level up, to the chain form: "every generator occurs in exactly one contiguous run", so that the closure is a linear connected sum of (2,k) torus links, is again a property of the assembly. With the confinement core alternating, a nucleon's letters no longer form two runs, so that reading of the block lapses. It is tempting to go further and say the block therefore satisfies this arc's own criterion for where many-body binding could live — "a closure that fails to be composite, non-split, prime, with the kind of irreducibly multi-component linking the Borromean rings have" — but that would be unsupported twice over: the block is a weighted sum of branch closures rather than one link, and containing \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} as a subword is not the same as being prime. What is actually measured is only that L is unchanged to \sim 10^{-60}: the reordering happens inside each nucleon, the nucleons remain strung on a chain, and no many-body binding appears anywhere.

What moves is every absolute trace: the intra factor falls by 3.8\times at ^2H to 14.3\times at ^4He when the confinement core is relaid alternating, carrying the difference-based B = Q_\beta\bigl(\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{free}}) - \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}})\bigr) route with it by the same factor.

The split is proved. Given the connected-sum input — \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}}) = F \prod_i (z + d_i) and \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{free}}) = F — the ratio is \prod_i (z+d_i) for any intra factor F \neq 0, so two orderings with factors F_1, F_2 give the same ratio with no hypothesis relating them , and hence the same L . The invariance is cancellation, not coincidence. The difference route instead satisfies F_1(1-P) = (F_1/F_2)\,F_2(1-P) and genuinely differs whenever F_1 \neq F_2 and P \neq 1. And the two confinement words are different objects: at q = 1, where both are elementary, the per-generator product is 1/4 and the Borromean closed form is 1 , so the 82\,\% gap at q_0 is not a deformation artefact. The connected-sum multiplicativity itself is taken as input (classical, cited below), not proved here. The effect of the reordering on the absolute traces, and which word is \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}, are numerical measurements.

What is proved, what is checked, what is cited

The factor algebra is proved: the affine law \mathrm{tr}_2(\sigma + d) = z + d from the level-2 Wenzl weights; the mirror factor z - h = 1/(q(q^2+1)) and \mathrm{tr}_2(\sigma)\,\mathrm{tr}_2(\sigma^{-1}) = 1/[2]_q^2, hence L_{pp} + L_{nn} = 2\log(q + q^{-1}); positivity of all three factors for q \ge 1; and that -\log of a product of positive factors is the sum of the -\logs. The factorisation of the H_{3A} trace is checked at A \le 4 and rests on the chain form (verified through A = 12) plus the connected-sum multiplicativity of the Markov trace, which is classical [birman1974] and is cited rather than proved here. Nothing here says which prime closure would carry many-body binding, or that one exists in the framework.
rem:torus-chain-pages-on-bring:
Remark The pages of the torus-knot components embed on Bring's surface, and their complements carry the Bring frame. Every knotted component of the canonical closure is a (2, 2g+1)-torus knot with g \in \{1, 2, 3\}, and a torus knot is fibered: its complement is an open book whose pages are Seifert surfaces of genus g sharing the knot as binding, with monodromy of order 2(2g+1) and a unimodular Seifert form, so H_1(\text{page}) is self-dual -- a frame with a dual frame. Since the cohomological embedding criterion that fixes the genus of Bring's surface is \operatorname{rank} H_1(\mathrm{Seifert}(T_{2,s})) = (s-1)/2 \le g at the forced g = 4, the pages of T(2,3), T(2,5) and T(2,7) all embed on Bring's surface, and T(2,9) is the last of the family that does (proved).

The complement of T(2, 2g+1) is the unit tangent bundle of the (2, 2g+1, \infty) triangle orbifold, \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\Delta(2, 2g+1, \infty); the link of the Bring cone is, canonically, the unit tangent bundle of Bring's curve, \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\Gamma_4 (Bézout gives the canonical embedding degree 6 = 2g - 2). Both therefore carry the global left-invariant frame \{X, Y, V\} -- geodesic, horocyclic, fibre rotation -- and two Reeb flows: V, whose orbits are the Seifert circles transverse to the pages, and X, whose closed orbits are closed geodesics of the base. This is the concrete form of the coordinate frame the osculating-circle pencil of a plane curve suggests and cannot itself supply, since that pencil lives on a curve and the closure is an isotopy class.

Two limits. The frame is the split real form \mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{R}), whereas the Reeb triad modelled on the Bring cone link elsewhere in this manuscript is the compact form \mathfrak{su}(2); a genus-4 unit tangent bundle has \widetilde{\mathrm{SL}_2} geometry and admits no 3-Sasakian structure, so which real form is intended there is a question for that lemma. And none of this reaches the twist: the framing datum the binding gap needs is the torsion integral, which neither the pages nor the circle pencil carry by themselves.
rem:frenet-framing-is-not-an-invariant:
Remark The torsion half is not an invariant: the Frenet self-linking of T(2,q) jumps by q at r = 4/(q^2+4). The chain result fixed the curvature half of Călugăreanu for the canonical closure: Milnor's infimum of total curvature over the isotopy class is 2\pi(2A+1). The refrain of the same thread was that the binding gap needs the other half -- a fractional framing scalar, i.e. twist, which the osculating circle is blind to. This remark says what that half can and cannot be, on a realisation of the component knots.

For a closed curve with a framing F, \mathrm{Lk}_F = \mathrm{Wr} + \mathrm{Tw}_F with \mathrm{Lk}_F \in \mathbb{Z}, and for the Frenet framing \mathrm{Tw}_F = \frac{1}{2\pi}\oint \tau\, ds. The infimum of total curvature over an isotopy class is an invariant (Milnor); total torsion has no extremal invariant, and neither has the writhe -- a helical perturbation of any arc moves both by an arbitrary amount inside the isotopy class. Measured on the standard torus embedding

  \gamma(t) = \bigl((1 + r\cos qt)\cos 2t,\; (1 + r\cos qt)\sin 2t,\; r\sin qt\bigr)

of T(2,q), q \in \{3, 5, 7\}, along r \in \{0.45, \dots, 0.02\} (mpmath quadrature, 24 digits): \int\kappa\, ds decreases monotonically to 4\pi (\int\kappa/4\pi from 1.34, 2.26, 3.27 down to 1.0003, 1.003, 1.014), the infimum approached and never attained; \oint\tau\, ds and \mathrm{Wr} both move across the family; and \mathrm{Wr} + \mathrm{Tw}_F is an integer at every r -- but not the same integer.

The jump

At t = \pi/q one has \cos qt = -1, \sin qt = 0, and with \rho = 1-r, c = \cos(2\pi/q), s = \sin(2\pi/q),

  \gamma'(\pi/q) \times \gamma''(\pi/q)
  \;=\;
  \bigl(q^2 r - 4\rho\bigr)\cdot\bigl(q r s,\; -q r c,\; -2\rho\,(c^2+s^2)\bigr),

so the curvature vanishes there exactly when r = r^* = 4/(q^2+4): 4/13, 4/29, 4/53 for the three component types. Since \cos qt = -1 at the q parameters (2k+1)\pi/q, the family crosses q inflection points at once; the Frenet normal flips at each, and the Frenet self-linking jumps by q: \mathrm{Lk}_F = -2q for r > r^* and -q for r < r^*, in all three families. The factorisation is exact, and the algebra (the cross product of velocity and acceleration, the inflection criterion, the three inflection radii, the inflection parameters and their injectivity) is proved.

What this closes

Even the integer half of Călugăreanu is a property of the curve: the Frenet framing is a framing of the embedding, discontinuous across an inflection, not a framing of the knot type. So no framing datum -- fractional or integral -- comes from the geometry of the isotopy class alone. Whatever fractional framing datum the aether carries is therefore a property of the algebra (the fractional twist q^{2c(\lambda)/n}), or of a canonical embedding (a Möbius-energy or ropelength minimiser), never of the knot type. That is the honest closure of the "missing half" question inside this thread: the half the geometry supplies invariantly is exactly the half already in hand, the curvature floor, and it is not the one the binding gap needs.

Scope

Per component, on one convenient embedding; no canonical embedding is chosen and no torsion number is compared with the aether's hull-exit window, because the principle says such a comparison has no invariant meaning. That the t = \pi/q inflections are the only ones in the family is observed (sampled \kappa_{\min} > 0 at every listed r), not proved; the differentiation behind \gamma'(\pi/q), \gamma''(\pi/q) is a symbolic computation and is not part of the proved algebra. Nothing here connects curvature or torsion to binding.
rem:pn-bond-cannot-be-extremal:
Remark The pn bond constant is a convex combination of the pp and nn constants, so it can never be extremal. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the three interface letters are \sigma + d with

  d_{pp} = 0, \qquad d_{nn} = -h, \qquad d_{pn} = -h\,(1 - \delta/2)/2,
  \qquad h = q - q^{-1},

and the third is exactly the weighted average of the first two:

  d_{pn} \;=\; \Bigl(\tfrac12 + \tfrac{\delta}{4}\Bigr) d_{pp}
             + \Bigl(\tfrac12 - \tfrac{\delta}{4}\Bigr) d_{nn},
  \qquad \text{weights summing to } 1,
  \text{ both non-negative iff } |\delta| \le 2 .

Since the two-strand trace is affine in the offset, \mathrm{tr}_2(\sigma + d) = z + d, an affine map sends that convex combination to the same convex combination, so z + d_{pn} lies strictly between z + d_{nn} and z + d_{pp}; and L = -\log(z+d) is strictly decreasing in d. Hence

  L_{pp} \;<\; L_{pn} \;<\; L_{nn}
  \qquad\text{for every } q > 0 \text{ and every } \delta \in (0,2).

Why it matters at A = 2

At two nucleons there is one bond, one word, and no ordering or arrangement convention to choose, so nothing mediates between the bond constants and the prediction:

system bond L \alpha L (MeV) reality
^2He pp 0.489899 2.0507 unbound, no bound diproton
^2H pn 0.676822 2.8332 bound, 2.22452 MeV
2n nn 0.907262 3.7978 unbound, no bound dineutron

Exactly one of the three binds, and it is pn. A constant that ranks binding strength must therefore put pn at an extreme — and a convex combination is never an extreme. The deuteron is assigned the middle value, and is also overshot by 1.274\times.

Nothing here is tunable. \delta = (q-1)^2(1-q^{-4})/3 equals 0.00138 at q_0, and would have to reach 2 — at q \approx 3.458 against q_0 = 1.10998 — before the convexity even breaks.

The caveat, before the conclusion

This arc's L carries no spin, and the real distinction is a spin one: the deuteron binds in the ^3S_1 triplet channel, and every ^1S_0 two-body system — pp, pn, nn alike — is unbound. A spinless bond constant cannot be expected to separate bound from unbound, and no claim is made that it should. What does not follow from the absence of spin is the order: nothing about lacking a spin channel requires the unbound nn system to be ranked above the bound pn one. That ranking comes from the averaging convention, and would survive into a spin-resolved theory that kept the same letter.

Not a contradiction with the np-pairing channel

The corpus's np preference does not live in the bond constants. It lives in the self-conjugate (2,2) \vdash 4 partition, as the categorical Wigner energy \Delta_{(2,2)} = m_e [3]_q [2]_q^2 = 6.2894 MeV of np pairing. That is a level-four object and there is no (2,2) partition of 2, so it supplies nothing at A = 2. The two statements are consistent — which is the difficulty, because it leaves the two-body ordering with nothing to rescue it.

The ordering result above constrains L, which is a free-energy difference; whether B = \alpha L is a binding energy at all is the separate open claim.

What would have to change

One of these, none of them settled here: the pn interface stops being an average over crossing sign, so that its letter falls outside the segment [d_{nn}, d_{pp}]; or the bond constant stops being what ranks binding, and a channel the two-body sector actually possesses carries the np preference; or the framework declares the bond constant channel-averaged and says explicitly what it averages over, since at A = 2 the ^1S_0 / ^3S_1 split is the entire content.

What is proved

The convex-combination identity, the strict betweenness of the offsets for 0 < \delta < 2, its transport through the affine trace, and the ordering L_{pp} < L_{pn} < L_{nn} itself are proved. Not proved, because it is empirical input: that only pn binds. The measurement, the \delta bound and the Wigner reading are numerical.
rem:bond-log-ratio-is-a-free-energy:
Remark The bond log-ratio is a free-energy difference; that it is the binding energy is a separate, open claim. The Markov trace at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) is a state sum. On H_2 the two Wedderburn blocks (2) and (1,1) carry Wenzl weights

  w_+ = \frac{[3]_q}{[3]_q + 1} = 0.752702113\ldots, \qquad
  w_- = \frac{1}{[3]_q + 1} = 0.247297887\ldots, \qquad
  w_+ + w_- = 1

(the normalisation is exact), so w is a genuine probability measure on the blocks, on which \sigma acts by the block eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}. The interface trace is therefore an expectation,

  \mathrm{tr}_2(\sigma + d) \;=\; \mathbb{E}_w[\lambda + d] \;=\; z + d,
  \qquad z = \frac{q^3}{q^2+1},

and since the canonical chain's Markov trace is exactly the product of these factors (the chain factorisation, measured to \sim 10^{-59}), the quantity the binding arc computes is

  L \;=\; \log\frac{Z_{\text{free}}}{Z_{\text{bonded}}}
    \;=\; \sum_{\text{interfaces}} -\log \mathbb{E}_w[\lambda + d_i],

The ring quantity is the product \prod_i (z + d_i) \in \mathbb{Q}(q); L is its comparison reading, the logarithm taken after evaluation (mass identity, comparison paragraph). Read that way, L is a free-energy difference in the standard sense — dimensionless, in units of kT, per-interface additive, and positive because every factor z + d lies in (0,1) at q_0.

This part is settled

The bond log-ratio L is exact for z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) and applies wherever the canonical Markov trace appears. The three constants are closed forms:

bond d z + d L = -\log(z+d)
pp 0 0.612688037146 0.489899384255
nn -h 0.403627738351 0.907262265533
pn d_{pn} 0.508229789377 0.676821592386

with L_{pp} = -\log z, L_{nn} = \log\bigl(q(q^2+1)\bigr) and L_{pp} + L_{nn} = 2\log[2]_q.

One caveat belongs with the identification: the observable is signed, since the (1,1) eigenvalue -q^{-1} is negative. So this is the free energy of a signed observable over a quasi-probability, not of a positive one, and the sign is exactly the \sigma / \sigma^{-1} split — the p/n distinction itself. Convexity intuitions imported from ordinary statistical mechanics need checking rather than assuming.

The separate claim, which is open

That B = \alpha L is the nuclear binding energy is an interpretation, not a result. It is recorded here as open, with the evidence that bears on it:

  • At A = 2, where no ordering or arrangement convention is in play, the ordering is wrong. L_{pp} < L_{pn} < L_{nn} is forced for every q and every \delta \in (0,2), because the pn letter is by construction the convex combination of the pp and nn letters (why). So the model ranks the unbound dineutron above the bound deuteron. The absence of a spin channel explains why a spinless constant cannot separate bound from unbound; it does not explain the order.
  • No sum over per-bond constants can have a valley of stability. B is then linear in Z for the chain and convex in Z for all pairs, so its maximum sits at an endpoint: the most bound isobar is always the most neutron-rich.
  • The chain delivers 31\,\% of ^4He (8.68 MeV against B_{\mathrm{AME}} = 28.2957), and no interface offset can close the gap — the required offset is 2.43\times more negative than the most negative letter the algebra has.

None of that shows L is the wrong quantity. It shows that the step from this free energy to an energy in MeV is not established, and the corpus's own working binding route is a different one (the Layer-1 canonical |\mathrm{tr}_M(q_0)| table, which reaches -0.16\,\% to +5.87\,\% on \mathrm{D}, \mathrm{T}, ^3He and ^4He).

Scope

No number changes. Every computation of L stands as a correct free-energy difference; only the identification of that difference with the binding energy is open. The all-pairs extension is a separate matter and is retired for a separate reason: its bond multiset does not determine a braid word at all (the ordering ambiguity).

Why the reading cannot supply the identification — prior to all three misses

The three bullets above are evidence about a formula. There is a prior fact about the reading, and it is an identity in q rather than a measurement at q_0.

A free energy is F = -kT\log Z with Z = \sum_i e^{-E_i/kT}. Every summand of a partition function is a positive Boltzmann factor, and that positivity is not decoration: it is what makes F a Legendre transform, hence what gives it an internal energy and an entropy at all. This state sum has two summands, carrying the \sigma-eigenvalues q on (2) and -q^{-1} on (1,1):

  \mathrm{tr}_2(\sigma + d) \;=\; w_+\,(q + d) \;+\; w_-\,(-q^{-1} + d).

The second is negative, for every bond. At q_0:

bond \lambda_+ + d \lambda_- + d z + d
pp 1.10997858275138 \mathbf{-0.90091828395574} 0.61268803714647
pn 1.00552033498165 \mathbf{-1.00537653172547} 0.50822978937674
nn 0.90091828395574 \mathbf{-1.10997858275138} 0.40362773835083

and no letter the algebra has repairs it at any q. Positivity needs d > q^{-1} > 0, while the interface letters are d \in \{0, -h/2, d_{pn}, -h\}, all non-positive — so the required offset is not merely outside the available range, it is on the other side of zero from all of it, for every q > 0. Hence no real E_- satisfies e^{-E_-} = -q^{-1} + d, and the (1,1) block has no energy.

So there is no U and no S for \alpha L to be, or to differ from. The free-energy reading does not supply the step to a binding energy, and could not have. The three misses are downstream of that, not independent of it.

The same algebra shows that L itself stands. The total z + d stays positive because the (2) block outweighs the (1,1) block, so L is real, exact and canonical wherever it appears, and the free-energy description is correct as this block states it: a free energy of a signed observable over a quasi-probability. What goes is the sentence after it. Whether \alpha L is a binding energy for some other reason is untouched and still open; what is settled is that this reading is not the reason.

A detail the algebra hands over: for pn the two block factors nearly cancel, (\lambda_+ + d_{pn}) + (\lambda_- + d_{pn}) = h + 2d_{pn} = h\delta/2 = 1.4380325618674\times10^{-4} exactly. The interface the binding arc turns on is the near-null vector of the unweighted block sum, and survives in z+d only because w_+ \neq w_-.

The general statements are proved for every q: the (1,1) summand is negative, so that block has no real energy; positivity would need d > q^{-1}; the admissible letters are non-positive; the pairing is positive but signed at each of the three letters; and the pn block sum is h\delta/2. The table values are measured at q_0.
prose:intro-lp-dual-jucys-murphy:
The linear-programming dual of the Frobenius positivity gate assigns a shadow price to each Wedderburn block V_\lambda of H_n(q). Because the Jucys–Murphy elements L_1, \dots, L_n \in H_n(q) generate the maximal commutative Gelfand–Tsetlin subalgebra and act by content scalars on Hoefsmit's seminormal basis, their symmetric polynomials provide an explicit algebraic basis for the LP-dual variables.

This section proves the central-element and hook-content trace identities for the Jucys–Murphy operators (including the Specht character trace and corner-removal recursion), establishes the invariance of the LP-dual program under the spin/transpose involution \lambda \mapsto \lambda', and derives the resulting second-order Wigner symmetry-energy coefficient and the jet-graded mass-endomorphism tower.
prop:jucys-murphy-central-elements-qou:
Proposition Elementary symmetric polynomials in Jucys–Murphy elements are central in H_n(q) with closed-form spectrum on each Wedderburn block. In the Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(q), with \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1, the multiplicative Jucys-Murphy elements

  J_1 \;=\; 1, \qquad J_{k+1} \;=\; \sigma_k\, J_k\, \sigma_k,
  \qquad k = 1, \ldots, n-1,

commute with each other. The elementary symmetric polynomials

  P_\ell \;:=\; e_\ell(J_1, J_2, \ldots, J_n)
  \;\in\; Z\bigl(H_n(q)\bigr)

lie in the centre and act on the Wedderburn block V_\lambda (for generic q) as the scalar

  c_\ell(\lambda) \;=\; e_\ell\!\left(\{q^{2c(\square)} :
    \square \in \lambda\}\right)

where c(\square) = j - i is the content of cell \square = (i,j).
prf:jucys-murphy-central-elements-qou:
Proof Proof of jucys murphy central elements qou. Write h = q - q^{-1}. The Hecke relation gives \sigma_k^{-1} = \sigma_k - h.

Step 1: JM elements commute. J_k lies in the subalgebra generated by \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{k-1}, so \sigma_j commutes with J_k for j \ge k+1. That \sigma_j also commutes with J_k for j \le k-2, and that the J_k commute pairwise, are the standard properties of multiplicative Jucys–Murphy elements, proved by induction on k from the braid and Hecke relations [mathas1999] (Ch. 3).

Step 2: Symmetric polynomials in the J_k are central. It suffices to show that each \sigma_k commutes with every symmetric polynomial in J_1, \ldots, J_n. By Step 1, \sigma_k commutes with J_j for j \ne k, k+1. Every symmetric polynomial is a polynomial in those J_j and in J_k + J_{k+1} and J_k J_{k+1}. So it is enough that \sigma_k commutes with these two. From J_{k+1} = \sigma_k J_k \sigma_k:

  \sigma_k J_k = J_{k+1}\sigma_k^{-1} = J_{k+1}\sigma_k - h J_{k+1},
  \qquad
  \sigma_k J_{k+1} = \sigma_k^2 J_k \sigma_k = h J_{k+1} + J_k \sigma_k,

and adding gives \sigma_k (J_k + J_{k+1}) = (J_k + J_{k+1})\sigma_k. Also \sigma_k J_k J_{k+1} = J_{k+1}\sigma_k^{-1}\,\sigma_k J_k \sigma_k = J_{k+1} J_k \sigma_k = J_k J_{k+1}\sigma_k, using Step 1. Hence P_\ell \in Z(H_n(q)) for all 1 \le \ell \le n.

Step 3: Spectrum on Wedderburn blocks. The seminormal basis \{v_T\}_T (T = standard Young tableau of shape \lambda) diagonalises every J_k:

  J_k v_T = q^{2 c(\square_k(T))}\, v_T

(at n = 2: J_2 = \sigma_1^2 has eigenvalues q^2 and q^{-2}, the contents \pm 1)

where \square_k(T) is the cell of T containing k and c(\square) = j - i. (This is the Hoefsmit–Wenzl formula; see Kassel 1995 §VI.6 for the H_n(q) version.)

The seminormal basis decomposes V_\lambda as a direct sum over standard tableaux of shape \lambda. Symmetric polynomials in \{q^{2c(\square_k(T))} : k = 1, \ldots, n\} depend only on the multiset of contents — which is the multiset \{c(\square) : \square \in \lambda\}, independent of the particular tableau T. Hence

  P_\ell v_T =
  e_\ell\!\left(\{q^{2c(\square)} : \square \in \lambda\}\right)
  v_T

acts as the same scalar c_\ell(\lambda) on every v_T of shape \lambda.

By Schur's lemma (each V_\lambda is irreducible), this is the unique scalar action of the central element P_\ell on V_\lambda. \square

Corollary (closed form for level-\ell corrections). The level-\ell correction to the QOU mass formula is the \tau-extraction of P_\ell restricted to height-(\ell{+}1) partitions:

  T^{(\ell)}(\varrho)
  \;=\; m_e \cdot \frac{
    \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3A,\, \mathrm{ht}(\lambda) = \ell+1}
      w_\lambda(q) \cdot c_\ell(\lambda)
  }{[3A]_q!}

where w_\lambda(q) = \dim_q(\lambda)^2 / [n]_q! is the Wedderburn weight and \mathrm{ht}(\lambda) is the number of non-zero parts.

Application: \alpha_5 derivation. For \ell = 5, ht=6, this gives

  \alpha_5 \;=\; m_e \cdot \frac{
    \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3A,\, \mathrm{ht}(\lambda) = 6}
      w_\lambda(q) \cdot c_5(\lambda)
  }{[3A]_q!}

a finite combinatorial sum over height-6 partitions of 3A. This is the simplest closed-form ansatz consistent with the iterative LP-dual characterisation of the mass formula; it is conjectural, not implied by the central-element theorem.

Empirical status. The companion numerical computation refutes this ansatz at \ell = 5: the relative spread of the normalised quantity across A \in \{2, 3, 4\} is \approx 482\% at q_0, and the spread is uniformly bad across the entire physical regime |q| \in (1, \varphi). The structural framework (Murphy 1992 + LP-dual extraction) is intact; the simplest closed form is not.
rem:jucys-murphy-central-elements-qou-in: Remark Jucys–Murphy elements as the Hecke shadow of commuting Casimirs. The Jucys-Murphy elements are the Hecke-algebraic shadow of commuting Casimirs in U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n). They are the natural commuting operators that read off the highest weight of an irreducible representation. The cell content c(\square) is the magnetic quantum number m_j of the corresponding \mathrm{SU}_q(2) weight space, making c_\ell(\lambda) a q-deformation of the \ell-th Casimir eigenvalue on V_\lambda. The crystal limit q \to 0 recovers the classical content combinatorics of the Kashiwara crystal.
lem:piece-a-hook-content-identity:
Lemma Piece A — the hook–content identity \sum_{\square} h(\square)^2 = \sum_{\square} c(\square)^2 + n^2. Let \lambda \vdash n be a partition, drawn as a Young diagram whose cells are \square = (i,j). Write

  h(\square) \;=\; \mathrm{arm}(\square) + \mathrm{leg}(\square) + 1,
  \qquad
  c(\square) \;=\; j - i

for the hook length and the content of \square. Then

  \sum_{\square \in \lambda} h(\square)^2
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\square \in \lambda} c(\square)^2 \;+\; n^2 .

The identity holds for every single partition — no averaging, no hook-length formula, and no reference to \dim S^\lambda or to the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda.
lem:piece-a-specht-character-trace:
Lemma Trace of the central element C_2 = \sum_i L_i^2 on S^\mu and on the regular representation. Let C_2 = \sum_{i} L_i^2 be the sum of the squared Jucys–Murphy elements, a central element of \mathbb{C}[S_n]. Then on the irreducible Specht module S^\mu,

  \mathrm{Tr}\bigl(C_2 |_{S^\mu}\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \dim\bigl(S^\mu\bigr) \cdot \sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2 ,

and on the full regular representation of S_n,

  \mathrm{Tr}(C_2)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\mu \vdash n}
    \Bigl( \sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2 \Bigr)
    \dim\bigl(S^\mu\bigr)^2 .
prf:piece-a-specht-character-trace:
Proof Proof of the C_2 traces on S^\mu and on the regular representation. C_2 is central, so by Schur's lemma [serre1977] it acts on the irreducible S^\mu by a scalar. That scalar is the common eigenvalue of \sum_i L_i^2 on the Gelfand–Tsetlin basis of S^\mu: each L_i acts on a basis vector indexed by a standard tableau T by the content of the cell holding i, so \sum_i L_i^2 acts by \sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2 — the same value for every T, as centrality requires. The restricted operator is therefore \bigl(\sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2\bigr) \cdot \mathrm{id}_{S^\mu}, and the trace of a scalar multiple of the identity is that scalar times the dimension:

  \mathrm{Tr}\bigl(C_2|_{S^\mu}\bigr)
  = \Bigl(\sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2\Bigr)\dim\bigl(S^\mu\bigr).

For the regular representation, decompose \mathbb{C}[S_n] by Artin–Wedderburn [sagan2001]: each S^\mu occurs with multiplicity \dim(S^\mu), so

  \mathbb{C}[S_n] \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\mu \vdash n}
    \bigl(S^\mu\bigr)^{\oplus \dim(S^\mu)} .

Trace is additive over that decomposition, and each summand contributes the value just computed, giving

  \mathrm{Tr}(C_2)
  = \sum_{\mu \vdash n}
     \dim\bigl(S^\mu\bigr) \cdot
     \Bigl(\sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2\Bigr) \dim\bigl(S^\mu\bigr)
  = \sum_{\mu \vdash n}
     \Bigl(\sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2\Bigr) \dim\bigl(S^\mu\bigr)^2 .

Dividing by n! = \sum_\mu \dim(S^\mu)^2 turns the right-hand side into the Plancherel expectation \mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{Planch}}\bigl[\sum_\square c(\square)^2\bigr], which is the form Piece B consumes. \blacksquare
lem:piece-a-corner-removal-obligation:
Lemma Corner-removal obligation: the hook-square change on removing a corner is (s-r)^2 + 2n - 1. Let \lambda \vdash n and let (r,s) be a removable corner, so s = \lambda_r - 1 and row r+1 is strictly shorter than row r. Write \mathrm{colLen}(j) for the number of rows reaching column j, and

  h(i,j) \;=\; (\lambda_i - j) + \bigl(\mathrm{colLen}(j) - i\bigr) - 1 .

Then the change in the hook-square sum caused by deleting the corner is

  1
  \;+\; \sum_{j=0}^{s-1}\bigl(2h(r,j) - 1\bigr)
  \;+\; \sum_{i=0}^{r-1}\bigl(2h(i,s) - 1\bigr)
  \;=\;
  (s-r)^2 \;+\; 2n - 1 .

The three terms on the left are the corner's own hook (which is 1), the cells of row r strictly left of the corner, and the cells of column s strictly above it — the only cells whose hook length changes.
prf:piece-a-corner-removal-obligation:
Proof Proof of the corner-removal obligation. Write R = \sum_{i<r} \lambda_i for the cells in the rows strictly above the corner and C = \sum_{j<s} \mathrm{colLen}(j) for the cells in the columns strictly left of it. The argument runs through five steps.

(L1) The corner's column has height r+1. \mathrm{colLen}(s) = \#\{i : \lambda_i > s\} = \#\{i : \lambda_i \geq \lambda_r\}. Row r reaches column s and row r+1 is strictly shorter, so by weak decrease the rows meeting that condition are exactly 0, \ldots, r:

  \mathrm{colLen}(s) \;=\; r + 1 .

(L2) Hooks along the corner row. For j < s, substituting \lambda_r - 1 = s into the definition,

  h(r,j) \;=\; (s - j) + \bigl(\mathrm{colLen}(j) - r\bigr).

(L3) Hooks along the corner column. For i < r, substituting \mathrm{colLen}(s) = r+1 from (L1),

  h(i,s) \;=\; (\lambda_i - s) + (r - i).

(L4) The row sum. By (L2), 2h(r,j) - 1 = 2(s-j) + 2\,\mathrm{colLen}(j) - 2r - 1. Summing over j = 0, \ldots, s-1 and using \sum_{j<s}(s-j) = \tfrac{1}{2}s(s+1),

  \sum_{j=0}^{s-1}\bigl(2h(r,j) - 1\bigr)
  \;=\; 2C + s^2 - 2rs .

(L5) The column sum. By (L3), 2h(i,s) - 1 = 2\lambda_i - 2s + 2r - 2i - 1. Summing over i = 0, \ldots, r-1 and using \sum_{i<r} i = \tfrac{1}{2}r(r-1),

  \sum_{i=0}^{r-1}\bigl(2h(i,s) - 1\bigr)
  \;=\; 2R + r^2 - 2sr .

(L6) Size decomposition. Split \lambda against the corner by inclusion–exclusion. The rows above the corner contribute R; the columns left of it contribute C; their overlap is the full r \times s rectangle, because every row i \leq r has \lambda_i \geq s+1 and so contains every column j < s. No cell lies in neither region except the corner itself: rows below r are strictly shorter than s+1, and row r has only j = s left. Hence

  n \;=\; R + C - rs + 1,
  \qquad\text{so}\qquad
  2(R + C) \;=\; 2n + 2rs - 2 .

Assembly. Adding the corner's own contribution 1 to (L4) and (L5),

  1 + \bigl(2C + s^2 - 2rs\bigr) + \bigl(2R + r^2 - 2sr\bigr)
  \;=\; 1 + 2(R+C) + r^2 + s^2 - 4rs .

Substituting (L6) for 2(R+C),

  1 + \bigl(2n + 2rs - 2\bigr) + r^2 + s^2 - 4rs
  \;=\; 2n - 1 + r^2 - 2rs + s^2
  \;=\; (s-r)^2 + 2n - 1 . \qquad \blacksquare
prop:spin-involution-lp-dual-invariance:
Proposition Spin involutions on Frobenius algebras leave the LP-dual shadow price invariant: \sigma(c) = c \Rightarrow y_0^*(\sigma(\beta)^*) = y_0^*(\beta). Let (A, \tau) be a Frobenius algebra with an involution * and a spin involution \sigma commuting with *. Let c \in A be \sigma-invariant. Let \Sigma be a \sigma-stable set of central idempotents of A. For any \beta \in A, the optimal dual variable y_0^* of the operator-selection LP

  \min_{x \in A}\; \tau(c \cdot x)
  \quad \text{s.t.} \quad
  \tau(\beta^* \beta \cdot x) = n_{\mathrm{target}}(\beta), \;\;
  \tau(\pi_\lambda \cdot x) \geq 0 \;\; \forall \lambda \in \Sigma

Suppose n_{\mathrm{target}}(\sigma(\beta)^*) = n_{\mathrm{target}}(\beta). Then

  y_0^*\bigl(\sigma(\beta)^*\bigr) \;=\; y_0^*(\beta).
prf:spin-involution-lp-dual-invariance:
Proof Proof of spin involution lp dual invariance. Step 1 — Frobenius pairing is σ-symmetric. The Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle_\tau := \tau(ab) satisfies, for all a, b \in A:

  \langle \sigma(a), \sigma(b) \rangle_\tau
  = \tau(\sigma(a)\sigma(b))
  = \tau(\sigma(ba))
  = \tau(ba)
  = \langle b, a \rangle_\tau
  = \langle a, b \rangle_\tau,

where the second equality is anti-multiplicativity, the third is trace-invariance, and the last is symmetry of \tau (the Markov / cyclic property). Hence \sigma is an isometry of the Frobenius pairing.

Step 2 — σ stabilises the constraint cone. Since \Sigma is \sigma-stable, the polyhedral cone \mathcal{K}_+ := \{x \in A : \tau(\pi_\lambda \cdot x) \geq 0\ \forall \lambda \in \Sigma\} satisfies \sigma(\mathcal{K}_+) = \mathcal{K}_+ (apply Step 1 to each constraint).

Step 3 — σ stabilises the cost functional. Because \sigma(c) = c and \tau \circ \sigma = \tau:

  \tau(c \cdot \sigma(x))
  = \tau(\sigma(\sigma(c) \cdot x))
  = \tau(\sigma(c \cdot x))
  = \tau(c \cdot x).

The cost is \sigma-invariant: replacing x by \sigma(x) does not change the objective.

Step 4 — σ relates the two LPs. Define \mathrm{LP}(\beta) to be the LP with input \beta. The net constraint \tau(\beta^* \beta \cdot x) = n_{\mathrm{target}}(\beta) transforms under x \mapsto \sigma(x) to

  \tau(\beta^* \beta \cdot \sigma(x))
  = \tau\bigl(\sigma(\sigma(\beta^*\beta) \cdot x)\bigr)
  = \tau\bigl(\sigma(\beta^*\beta) \cdot x\bigr)
  = \tau\bigl(\sigma(\beta)\,\sigma(\beta)^* \cdot x\bigr),

where the first equality uses anti-multiplicativity and \sigma^2 = \mathrm{id}, the second uses \tau \circ \sigma = \tau, and the third uses \sigma(\beta^*\beta) = \sigma(\beta)\,\sigma(\beta^*) = \sigma(\beta)\,\sigma(\beta)^* (anti-multiplicativity, and \sigma commuting with *). Put \beta' = \sigma(\beta)^*; then \beta'^*\beta' = \sigma(\beta)\,\sigma(\beta)^*, so the transformed constraint is the net constraint of \mathrm{LP}(\beta'). By the hypothesis n_{\mathrm{target}}(\beta') = n_{\mathrm{target}}(\beta), \sigma is a bijection between the feasible sets of \mathrm{LP}(\beta) and \mathrm{LP}(\beta'), preserving the objective. In general \sigma(\beta)\,\sigma(\beta)^* \neq \sigma(\beta)^*\sigma(\beta), so this does not relate \mathrm{LP}(\beta) to \mathrm{LP}(\sigma(\beta)).

Step 5 — LP-duality. By Steps 2–4, \mathrm{LP}(\beta) and \mathrm{LP}(\sigma(\beta)^*) have feasible sets in \sigma-bijection and the same \sigma-invariant cost; their primal optima coincide. By strong duality (which holds for Frobenius algebras structurally — see Frobenius self-duality of (H_n(R,q),\tau) forces \tau-extraction to produce LP-dual variables), the dual optima coincide. In particular,

  y_0^*\bigl(\sigma(\beta)^*\bigr) = y_0^*(\beta). \qquad\square

Corollary (QOU instance — isospin invariance; NOT established). For A = H_n(R, q) with \tau the Markov trace and \sigma = S the Hopf antipode, the per-atom canonical braid recipe satisfies S(\mathcal{B}_K(Z, N)) \sim \mathcal{B}_K(N, Z) (Markov- conjugate). Consequently, for every central cost operator c \in Z(H_n(q)) (in particular c = P_\ell = e_\ell(J_1, \ldots, J_n), Murphy 1992) and every \sigma-stable Wedderburn stratum \Sigma,

  y_0^*(Z, N) = y_0^*(N, Z).

Status. The argument that stood here fails at its first step. It asserted that \tau is S-invariant for the antipode S(\sigma_i) = \sigma_i^{-1}. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), \tau(\sigma_i) = z = q^3/(q^2+1), while \tau(\sigma_i^{-1}) = \tau(\sigma_i) - (q - q^{-1}) = 1/\bigl(q(q^2+1)\bigr); at q_0 these are 0.6127 and 0.4036. Moreover \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} does not preserve the Hecke relation over R: the image satisfies (\sigma_i^{-1} - q^{-1})(\sigma_i^{-1} + q) = 0, the relation at q^{-1}. It is an algebra map only together with q \mapsto q^{-1}, i.e. the bar involution, and \tau is bar-equivariant, \tau(\bar x) = \overline{\tau(x)}, not invariant. So the hypothesis \tau \circ \sigma = \tau of the proposition is not met by the Markov trace with this \sigma, and y_0^*(Z, N) = y_0^*(N, Z) does not follow. The R-linear anti-automorphism T_w \mapsto T_{w^{-1}} does preserve \tau, but it fixes every generator and so does not exchange Z and N.

prop:wigner-2-coefficient:
Proposition Wigner-2 coefficient C_{[3,2,1]} = w_{[3,2,1]} \cdot h/2 from self-conjugate trace pairing. For any self-conjugate partition \lambda = \lambda' of k, the per-generator trace in the Hoefsmit seminormal representation evaluates to:

  \frac{\mathrm{tr}(\sigma_g^{(\lambda)})}{\dim(\lambda)}
  = \frac{h}{2}
  = \frac{q - q^{-1}}{2}.

Consequently, the BW shadow-price coefficient for \lambda is:

  C_\lambda = w_\lambda \cdot \frac{h}{2}
  = \frac{\dim_q(\lambda)^2}{[k]_q!} \cdot \frac{q - q^{-1}}{2}.
prf:wigner-2-coefficient:
Proof Proof of wigner 2 coefficient. The argument has three steps: a pairing identity, a counting argument, and an algebraic simplification.

Step 1 (Paired sum identity). In the seminormal form, the diagonal entry for standard tableau T at generator \sigma_g is a_\rho = h/(1 - q^{-2\rho}) where \rho = c(T, g{+}1) - c(T, g) is the axial distance (difference of contents of the cells containing entries g{+}1 and g).

For any \rho \neq 0:

  a_\rho + a_{-\rho}
  = \frac{h}{1 - q^{-2\rho}} + \frac{h}{1 - q^{2\rho}}
  = h \cdot \frac{(1 - q^{2\rho}) + (1 - q^{-2\rho})}
              {(1 - q^{-2\rho})(1 - q^{2\rho})}
  = h \cdot \frac{2 - q^{2\rho} - q^{-2\rho}}
              {1 - q^{2\rho} - q^{-2\rho} + 1}
  = h

since numerator and denominator are both 2 - (q^{2\rho} + q^{-2\rho}).

Step 2 (Conjugation pairing). Let \lambda = \lambda' be self-conjugate. The transposition of the Young diagram (reflecting across the main diagonal) induces an involution T \mapsto T^\vee on the set of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda. Under this involution:

  • The cell of entry m in T^\vee has content -c(T, m) (reflection swaps row and column).
  • Therefore \rho(T^\vee, g) = -\rho(T, g) for every generator g.
  • Since \lambda is self-conjugate, T^\vee is again a valid SYT of shape \lambda.
  • The involution is fixed-point-free on axes: \rho(T,g) \neq 0 implies T^\vee \neq T in the relevant entry positions.

The \dim(\lambda) tableaux pair into \dim(\lambda)/2 conjugate pairs \{T, T^\vee\}.

Step 3 (Trace computation). The trace of \sigma_g in the seminormal basis is the sum of all diagonal entries:

  \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_g^{(\lambda)})
  = \sum_{T} a_{\rho(T,g)}
  = \sum_{\{T, T^\vee\}} \bigl(a_{\rho(T,g)} + a_{-\rho(T,g)}\bigr)
  = \sum_{\{T, T^\vee\}} h
  = \frac{\dim(\lambda)}{2} \cdot h

Dividing by \dim(\lambda):

  \frac{\mathrm{tr}(\sigma_g^{(\lambda)})}{\dim(\lambda)}
  = \frac{h}{2}

This is independent of g (since all generators are conjugate in S_k, and the trace is conjugation-invariant).

Corollary (BW coefficient). By the shadow price proposition, C_\lambda = w_\lambda \cdot \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_g)/\dim. Substituting \mathrm{tr}/\dim = h/2:

  C_\lambda = \frac{\dim_q(\lambda)^2}{[k]_q!} \cdot \frac{h}{2}

For \lambda = [3,2,1] \vdash 6, the hook lengths are \{5, 3, 1, 3, 1, 1\}, giving \dim_q = [6]_q!/([5]_q [3]_q^2) = [2]_q [4]_q [6]_q / [3]_q. Therefore:

  C_{[3,2,1]}
  = \frac{[2]_q^2 [4]_q^2 [6]_q^2}{[3]_q^2 \cdot [6]_q!}
    \cdot \frac{h}{2}
  = \frac{[2]_q [4]_q [6]_q \cdot h}{2\,[3]_q^3\,[5]_q}

rem:quantum-dilogarithm-stratified-parti:
Remark Partial argument for the stratified quantum dilogarithm. Partial argument for the stratified quantum dilogarithm conjecture. Steps 1, 2 and 4 below are argued; Step 3 is not established, and as written it cannot be: F_n(z) in (d) is a single power of z, so the product expansion F_n(z) = \prod_k (1 - q^{-k}z)^{-c_k(n)}\, u_n(q) fails for it. What is proved is Step 1, the mutual orthogonality of the depth strata under the Frobenius pairing.

Step 1 (Frobenius dual decomposition of Z(A)). Partitioning the primitive central idempotents e_\lambda (\lambda \vdash n) by the max-hook statistic \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) := \max_{\square \in \lambda} h(\square), the centre Z(A) = \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} R \cdot e_\lambda decomposes directly into vector-space strata Z(A) = \bigoplus_{k \geq 0} Z^{(k)}(A), where Z^{(k)}(A) := \bigoplus_{\mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) = k} R \cdot e_\lambda (this partition-level grading is definitional and does not rely on the word-level filtration of curvature-rank stratification, whose relation to partition hook length is examined in Step 3(b) below). The Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle = \int_A a \cdot b restricts to Z(A) as a non-degenerate bilinear form, and the depth strata Z^{(k)}(A) are mutually orthogonal under this pairing:

  \langle Z^{(k)}(A),\, Z^{(\ell)}(A) \rangle \;=\; 0
  \qquad \text{whenever } k \neq \ell .

The pairing of strata is diagonal. The strata are spans of central primitive idempotents, and distinct idempotents annihilate each other: for any linear functional \varphi, \varphi(e_\lambda e_\mu) = \varphi(\delta_{\lambda\mu} e_\lambda). So the pairing on that basis is \mathrm{diag}(\tau(e_\lambda)), with every stratum self-dual and every distinct pair annihilating; at n = 3 this holds exactly in \mathbb{Q}(q) (all six off-diagonal entries vanish, the diagonal is nonzero, and \sum_\lambda \tau(e_\lambda) = 1). This is the form Step 4 needs: it uses \langle Z^{(k)}, Z^{(\ell)}\rangle = 0 for k \neq \ell, which an anti-diagonal (Poincaré-type) duality Z^{(k)} \times Z^{(N-k)} \to R would not supply.

Open: Step 4 pairs a central \phi_q^{(k)} against a general T_w \in A, not against a central element, so "T_w has zero projection on Z^{(k)}" has to be read as a statement about T_w's Wedderburn blocks. That reading is plausible, since for a central idempotent \tau(e_\lambda a) = \tau(e_\lambda a e_\lambda), but it is not stated in the block.

where N is the maximal GB-depth in Z(A), retained below only as the top of the depth range. The pairing Z^{(k)} \times Z^{(k)} \to R is non-degenerate on each stratum separately — each stratum is self-dual, and there is no Poincaré-type pairing across distinct strata.

Step 2 (existence of \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i)). By cor: quantum dilogarithm, the level-i torsion-volume contribution to the mass is \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) = \Phi_q(z_i). Since the mass functional is centre-valued by categorical mass = Markov trace, the \Phi_q(z_i)-action on Z(A) via the Markov pairing factors through Z(A). Decomposing along the depth grading,

  \Phi_q(z_i) \cdot \mathrm{id}_{Z(A)}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{k \geq 0} \Phi_q(z_i) \cdot \mathrm{proj}_{Z^{(k)}(A)}.

Define \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i) := \mathrm{proj}_{Z^{(k)}(A)}(\Phi_q(z_i)) as the depth-k projection of the Frobenius dual.

Step 3 (cyclotomic factors \leftrightarrow depth-k partitions). The cyclotomic factor (1 - q^{-k} z_i)^{-1} in \Phi_q(z_i) has its pole locus at z_i = q^k. This locus is identified with the depth-k centre stratum Z^{(k)}(A) via the q-content / hook-length structure:

(a) The q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight is w_\lambda(q) = \dim_q^2 V_\lambda / [n]_q! (distinct from the classical Plancherel measure w_\lambda(1) = (\dim V_\lambda)^2/n! — the two coincide at q = 1), where \dim_q V_\lambda = [n]_q! \,/\, \prod_{\square \in \lambda} [h(\square)]_q and [h]_q = (q^h - q^{-h})/(q - q^{-1}) is the symmetric quantum integer (Hoefsmit pipeline).

(b) The hook lengths h(\square) for \square \in \lambda define the partition's max-hook depth in Z(A). Here \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) = \max_{\square \in \lambda} h(\square) (the partition's maximum hook length) is a definition — the supremum of the hook length over the cells of \lambda — not a consequence of curvature-rank stratification, which is a conjecture stratifying J^{\,r}/J^{\,r+1} by the curvature rank r(T_w) of words and mentions no partition. The two are different indexings of depth, and reading \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) as the minimal number of R_H, R_{YB} rewrites needed to put any element of the \lambda-isotypic component in NF requires an identification of the partition grading with the word filtration that that conjecture does not supply.

(c) Therefore \dim_q V_\lambda has a factor of [k]_q in its hook-length expansion exactly when \lambda contains a box with h(\square) = k, equivalently \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) \geq k. Under the substitution z_i \to q^k, the factor [k]_q vanishes — \dim_q V_\lambda(q)\big|_{z_i = q^k} has a zero, and the corresponding w_\lambda(q)^{-1} specialisation has a pole.

(d) The Markov-trace generating function for the centre is the formal series F_n(z) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \dim_q^{-1}(V_\lambda) \cdot z^{|\lambda|}, and its expansion as an infinite product in z is F_n(z) = \prod_{k \geq 1} (1 - q^{-k} z)^{-c_k(n)} \cdot u_n(q) where c_k(n) = \#\{\lambda \vdash n : \max\text{-hook}(\lambda) = k\} and u_n(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] is a unit. The exponent c_k(n) counts depth-exactly-k partitions; the factor (1 - q^{-k} z)^{-c_k(n)} contributes the depth-k stratum of Z(A).

Scope of (d): the multi-factor product expansion does not hold for a homogeneous monomial. Every \lambda \vdash n has |\lambda| = n, so F_n(z) = \bigl(\sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \dim_q^{-1}(V_\lambda)\bigr)\, z^n is a single monomial in z. A product \prod_{k \geq 1}(1-q^{-k}z)^{-c_k(n)}\, u_n(q) with some c_k(n) > 0 has the nonzero z^1 coefficient u_n(q)\sum_k c_k(n)\, q^{-k} when n \geq 2, so the two sides cannot agree. Steps (e)–(f) inherit this. The proved truncation statement is Cell-depth truncation of a trace.

(e) The single-stratum factor (1 - q^{-k}z)^{-1} in \Phi_q is the c_k = 1 specialisation of (d) — applicable when each depth-k stratum is one-dimensional or when factoring over irreducible strata. For the brane-tower, each exceptional divisor p_i contributes one (1 - q^{-k} z_i)^{-1} per depth k, and the full \Phi_q(z_i) = \prod_k (1 - q^{-k} z_i)^{-1} is the universal generating function over all depths.

(f) Combining (a)–(e): the partial product \Phi_q^{[\leq k]}(z_i) = \prod_{j=1}^{k}(1-q^{-j}z_i)^{-1} generates exactly the contributions from depths 1, 2, \ldots, k, and the truncation increment \Phi_q^{[\leq k]}(z_i) - \Phi_q^{[\leq k-1]}(z_i) is the depth-exactly-k generator. Identifying this with the Frobenius dual \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i) from Step 2 (modulo orthogonal strata) gives

  \Phi_q^{[\leq k]}(z_i) - \Phi_q^{[\leq k-1]}(z_i)
  \;\equiv\; \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i) \pmod{\bigoplus_{\ell \neq k} Z^{(\ell)}(A)}.

Step 4 (Frobenius truncation for T_w). For T_w \in H_n(R, q) with NF support depth k_\star(T_w) = \max_{\lambda \in \mathrm{supp}(T_w)} \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda), T_w has zero projection on Z^{(k)}(A) for every k > k_\star(T_w) by definition of k_\star. By Step 3, \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i) \in Z^{(k)}(A), so

  \bigl\langle \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i),\, T_w \bigr\rangle \;=\; 0
  \qquad \text{for } k > k_\star(T_w).

The Frobenius-paired sum truncates:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_q(z_i) \cdot T_w\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{k = 0}^{\infty} \bigl\langle \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i),\, T_w \bigr\rangle
  \;=\;
  \sum_{k = 0}^{k_\star(T_w)} \bigl\langle \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i),\, T_w \bigr\rangle
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i) \cdot T_w\bigr).

The second equality uses depth orthogonality (Step 1); the third uses Step 3's identification of the partial product with the \bigoplus_{j \leq k_\star(T_w)} Z^{(j)}-content.

Open: canonical bound. The proof above is a Frobenius-paired equality, not a canonical identity. It says the Frobenius-pairing of \Phi_q(z_i) with T_w equals the Frobenius-pairing of \Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i) with T_w. To conclude that the canonical mass formula evaluated with \Phi_q replaced by \Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]} gives the same answer, one needs the projections \mathrm{proj}_{Z^{(k)}}(\Phi_q(z_i)) to be uniformly bounded as |z_i| \to q — equivalently, no spurious analytic mass leaks into Z^{(k)}(A) from the divergent infinite product. Establishing this uniform bound is the conjectural target of z-Habiro completion. It is no longer needed for \Phi_q categorical truncation: the level-wise \Phi_q identity that the bound was meant to regularise is false algebraically, and the centre-projection truncation is proved without it (Cell-depth truncation of a trace). Note also that with \Phi_q(z_i) a scalar the equality \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_q(z_i)T_w)=\mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_q^{[\le k_\star]}(z_i)T_w) fails at w=e unless \prod_{j>k_\star}(1-q^{-j}z_i)^{-1}=1, which is false for z_i\ne0; the statement above needs \Phi_q(z_i) read as a central element, and that reading is not fixed here.

The argument above establishes Step 1's categorical (Frobenius-paired) orthogonality of the partition strata Z^{(k)}(A), while leaving two independent gaps in Step 3 and the analytic limit: first, Step 3(a)–(c) uses the definitional max-hook statistic \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) = \max_{\square \in \lambda} h(\square), whereas curvature-rank stratification filters H_n(R, q) by word curvature rank r(T_w) without establishing the word-to-partition identification; second, the product expansion F_n(z) = \prod_k (1 - q^{-k}z)^{-c_k(n)} \cdot u_n(q) asserted in (d) is false for n \geq 2 because F_n(z) is a single homogeneous monomial in z (see the scope note under (d)), so unique factorisation in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}][z] supplies no such infinite-product identity.
rem:ks-finiteness-via-diamond-lemma: Remark Algebraic shortcut: Kontsevich--Soibelman's ind-constructibility from the Diamond Lemma. Kontsevich-Soibelman must assume ind-constructibility to measure their 3CY moduli stacks. The QOU framework avoids this assumption completely. The Gröbner-Shirshov confluent normal forms guarantee a finite basis of standard monomials at every length. The length slices construct finite-dimensional schemes immediately. The topological structure extracts rigorous finiteness directly from the Diamond Lemma.
def:delta-q-decoration:
Definition q-dimension decoration \delta_q : H_n(q) \to R^{|\mathrm{Par}(n)|} of the NF basis. The \delta_q-decoration maps an algebra element b \in H_n(q) to the tuple of its q-characters across each irreducible representation V_\lambda:

  \delta_q(b)
  \;:=\;
  \bigl(\chi_\lambda(b)\bigr)_{\lambda \vdash n}
  \;\in\;
  R^{|\,\mathrm{Par}(n)\,|}.

Its codomain is the q-dimension layer.
def:q-dimension-layer:
Definition q-dimension layer R^{|\mathrm{Par}(n)|}: per-irrep target of the \delta_q-decoration. The q-dimension layer is the codomain R^{|\mathrm{Par}(n)|} of the \delta_q-decoration, with one coordinate per partition \lambda \vdash n:

  R^{|\,\mathrm{Par}(n)\,|}
  \;=\;
  \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} R,
  \qquad
  b \longmapsto \bigl(\chi_\lambda(b)\bigr)_{\lambda \vdash n}.
rem:q-dimension-layer-remark: Remark What the q-dimension layer retains. The layer preserves the per-irrep structure that the Markov trace normally collapses. It provides the high-fidelity projection data required to map force-carrier knots into exact Wedderburn components. For example, it extracts the [9]_q and [10]_q q-dimensions for the Bring torus-knot force carriers directly from the character evaluations.
def:torus-knot-top-channel-decoration:
Definition Top-channel decoration \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p}) = q^{w} - q^{-w} of a torus knot. Let T_{m,p} be a positive torus knot presented on its braid index, so that m \le p, as the closure of the braid \beta_{m,p} = (\sigma_1\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_{m-1})^{p} \in B_m. Its writhe is w = (m-1)p. In the trivial one-dimensional representation of H_m(q), where every \sigma_i acts by q, the braid acts by q^{w}. The top-channel decoration of T_{m,p} is the bar-odd part of this eigenvalue under the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1}:

  \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p})
  \;:=\;
  q^{w} - q^{-w},
  \qquad
  w = (m-1)p.
rem:torus-knot-top-channel-decoration-re:
Remark Braid-index condition and comparison with the q-dimension decoration. The braid-index condition m \le p is part of the definition. T_{m,p} and T_{p,m} are the same knot, but (m-1)p \ne (p-1)m when m \ne p, so without the condition one knot would receive two values.

This is a scalar in R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. It is a different object from the q-dimension decoration \delta_q(b) = (\chi_\lambda(b))_{\lambda \vdash n}, which is a tuple of characters, and it is not the sum of that tuple. The two agree for m = 2: for odd p the characters of \beta_{2,p} = \sigma_1^{p} on V_{(2)} and V_{(1,1)} are q^{p} and (-q^{-1})^{p} = -q^{-p}, whose sum is q^{p} - q^{-p}. They disagree for m = 3. For T_{3,5} the characters of (\sigma_1\sigma_2)^{5} on V_{(3)}, V_{(2,1)}, V_{(1,1,1)} are q^{10}, -1, q^{-10}, whose sum is q^{10} - 1 + q^{-10}, while \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5}) = q^{10} - q^{-10}.
prop:alpha-basis-knot-delta-q:
Proposition q-dimension decoration of the basis knots: \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,k}) = h\,[k]_q. For the basis torus knot T_{2,k} (k odd), the top-channel decoration evaluates exactly as:

  \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,k}) \;=\; q^{k} - q^{-k} \;=\; h\,[k]_q.

The identity holds purely algebraically in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, h^{-1}] with no archimedean approximation.
